human_tolerance.notes: A familiar visitor to suburban gardens and woodland edges, feeding on the ground and in low shrubs and holding a territory by song all year.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Territory-holding males sing through the spring and summer; two to four clutches of three to four eggs are laid between March and August, with 12-13 days of incubation.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Non-breeding adults pair up for the winter and sing to hold the territory, both to defend it and in the winter dawn and dusk song.

vocalizations.description: Clear, slurred whistled phrases - cheer cheer cheer, cheer-cheer - repeated several times and then varied; both sexes sing, and the male marks his territory with it.
A short, sharp, metallic chip, given as a contact or alarm note.

range.note: Resident across the eastern United States into southern Canada, with the range extending south through Mexico to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec and into northern Guatemala and Belize; also established in Hawaii and Puerto Rico, which are not listed as native here.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Perching songbird: it walks and hops on the ground and perches, and flies between perches.

traits.nest_type.note: A bulky cup nest of twigs and grasses built in a shrub or low tree.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 42.64 g converted to kilograms.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Judgement band either side of the EltonTraits mean; no allow-listed open source states the mass range for this species.

traits.length_m.note: Body length of 21-23 cm; the midpoint of that range is used.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 25-31 cm wingspan given on Wikipedia.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia states the oldest wild cardinal banded by researchers lived at least 15 years and 9 months. That is a documented maximum, not a typical lifespan, and is used here as the best available figure; typical wild longevity is lower.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-PlantO 70 mapped to 'seed' (the dataset classes this species as PlantSeed), Diet-Fruit 10 to 'fruit', Diet-Inv 20 to 'invertebrate'. Wikipedia describes a granivorous bird that also takes insects and fruit in summer.

traits.social.note: The male holds a territory by song and the pair stays together; a mated pair is the usual social unit, and groups larger than two only form where food concentrates.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0; Wikipedia describes daytime territorial song and winter dawn and dusk singing.

traits.defense.note: Flies from an approaching threat and gives the metallic chip alarm call; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold and habituated to people, feeding in gardens and at feeders well inside its flight distance, but still leaves cover readily when closely approached.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value gives ground 40 / midhigh 20 / canopy 20 / understory 20; the arboreal share is the sum of the midhigh, canopy and understory strata.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and shelters in dense shrubbery and low tree cover.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the shelter and nesting weights are judgement, since no open source gives their relative importance.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia lists its natural habitat as woodlands, gardens, shrublands and wetlands and describes it as a familiar bird around human dwellings.

seasonal.strategy.note: A permanent resident across most of its United States range, with no migration.

seasonal.phases.note: Clutch size, number of clutches per year, incubation length and the year-round territorial song are from Wikipedia's breeding section; the split into breeding and non-breeding windows is authored judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Fledging is about 12-13 days after hatching; the 60-day juvenile window and the 0.85 scale are authored judgement.

vocalizations.song.note: Description from Wikipedia's Communication section; the dawn and dusk windows and the cooldown are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.chip.note: Wikipedia describes a distinctive short metallic chip as the alarm call; the cooldown is authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of the male's bright red plumage with a black face mask and a prominent crest; proportions and the crest and mask boxes are authored judgement to render the crest and mask.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: it flees 6 m to a perch, feeds on seed, sings and gives the chip alarm call, and nests between March and June.
